info.title: GitLocus evaluation service
info.description:
A pure evaluator. It stores nothing, reads no clock and makes no network call of its own, because a verdict is a pure function of (policy, contribution, evidence). The same evaluation runs in the `locus` CLI out of the same crate, so a verdict from here and a verdict from the command line cannot disagree.

There is no authentication because there is nothing to protect: no state, no secrets, no side effects. The answer is one the caller could compute themselves with the CLI.

get.summary: Liveness, and which version is answering.

post.summary: Evaluate a contribution against a policy.
post.description: Send `governing_policy` whenever the base revision has one. Without it a contribution is judged only by the document it ships, so a change that deletes the rule blocking it is judged by a policy that no longer contains that rule. The response reports `governed_by_base` so a caller who forgot can notice from the answer rather than from the documentation.

200.description: The contribution was evaluated. A `blocked` decision is a successful evaluation: the status code describes the request, not the contribution.

400.description: The request, the policy or the contribution could not be read.

413.description: The body exceeds the size limit. Bodies are refused rather than truncated: truncating would hand the evaluator a document the caller did not send.

policy.description: The policy at the revision under evaluation, as YAML.

governing_policy.description: The policy at the base revision, as YAML. Omit only when the base revision genuinely has no policy.

items.description: See spec/schemas/evidence.schema.json. A `signer` present here is ignored: a signer is a conclusion a verifier reaches, never a claim a document makes.

governed_by_base.description: Whether a base-revision policy was supplied and applied. Its absence changes what the verdict means.
